author: v😉😉😉
title: Deceiving
content:
I have played DoubleDown for several years and have spent thousands of dollars on the app, regularly purchasing chip packages priced at approximately $110. Recently, a package that I recognized and had previously purchased was charged at nearly $300. I completed the transaction before noticing the price discrepancy. I contacted DoubleDown promptly to request a review and adjustment, but the company refused to reconsider the charge solely because I had used some of the chips, despite my longstanding history as a paying customer.

I am also concerned about the transparency and fairness of the game’s operation. Over time, I have observed what appears to be a pattern in which my winnings decrease after I reach certain spending or account-balance levels. Losses then continue until my chips are depleted, after which the pattern appears to reset. I cannot independently verify whether winnings are restricted or linked to spending, but the repeated nature of this experience has caused me to question whether the game operates in a genuinely random and fair manner.

DoubleDown should provide clear, upfront pricing and disclose how jackpots, payouts, and winning outcomes are determined. Charging nearly $300 for a package commonly priced at approximately $110, followed by a refusal to meaningfully review the transaction, is unfair and potentially deceptive. I accept responsibility for the purchases I made, but the company also has a responsibility not to take advantage of loyal customers through unclear pricing, inadequate transaction disclosures, or gambling-style mechanics that may encourage continued spending.
